simple.meaning: נֹגַהּ (nôgahh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “brilliancy (literally or figuratively).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 19 times across 2 Samuel, Psalms, Proverbs, Isaiah, Ezekiel, and 3 more, beginning at 2 Samuel 22:13. Its contexts include righteousness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נֹגַהּ (H5051).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: נֹגַהּ (nôgahh) / H5051 is traced through 2 Samuel 22:13, 2 Samuel 23:4, Psalms 18:13, Proverbs 4:18 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: shall be as the light of the morning, when the sun rises,
Yahweh also thundered in the sky.
But the path of the righteous is like the dawning light
Yahweh will create over the whole habitation of Mount Zion and over her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night, for over all the glory will be a canopy.
Nations will come to your light,
The sun will be no more your light by day;
For Zion’s sake I will not hold my peace,

I looked, and behold,‡ “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection. a stormy wind came out of the north: a great cloud, with flashing lightning, and a brightness around it, and out of the middle of it as it were glowing metal, out of the middle of the fire.

As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of torches. The fire went up and down among the living creatures. The fire was bright, and lightning went out of the fire.

I saw as it were glowing metal, as the appearance of fire within it all around, from the appearance of his waist and upward; and from the appearance of his waist and downward I saw as it were the appearance of fire, and there was brightness around him.
As the appearance of the rainbow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness all around.
Yahweh’s glory mounted up from the cherub, and stood over the threshold of the house; and the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was full of the brightness of Yahweh’s glory.
Won’t the day of Yahweh be darkness, and not light?
His splendor is like the sunrise.
The sun and moon stood still in the sky,

definitions.full: H5051. nogah I. נֹ֫גַהּ noun feminine Hab 3:4 brightness ; — ׳נ absolute Amos 5:10 +; construct Isa 4:5 +; suffix נָגְהָם Joel 2:10 ; Joel 4:15; — brightness of a (clear, sunshiny) day Amos 5:10 (|| אוֺר ; opposed to חשֶׁךְ אָפֵל, ), 2Sam 23:4 ( מִמָּטָר after rain ); so figurative of Zion's dawning, ׳נ זַרְחֵךְ Isa 60:3 (|| אוֺר ); of her righteousness כַּנֹּגַהּ 62:1 (with article only here and Ezek 1:28 ), || יִבְעָ֑ר כְּלַמִּיד ; of moon Isa 60:19 , of stars Joel 2:10 ; Joel 4:15; of theophany 2Sam 22:13 = Psa 18:13 (in storm); compare Ezek 1:4 , 27 , 28 , ׳נ י ׳כְּבוֺד 10:4 ; ׳נ כאור Hab 3:4 ; ׳נ לָאֵשׁ Ezek 1:13 , ׳נ לֶהָבָה אֵשׁ Isa 4:5 ; חֲנִיתֶ֑ךָ ׳נ בְּרַק Hab 3:11 (of glitter of ׳י s spear; || חִצֶּיךָ אוֺר ); of individual, נ ׳וְאֵין לוֺ Isa 50:10 (figurative of distress || חֲשֵׁכִים ); so נ כְּאוֺר צַדִּיקִים ׳וְאֹרַח Prov 4:18 the path of righteous men is like a light of brightness.
